docs.title: Lab Objective
docs.text:
The objective of this lab is to provide hands-on experience with the Webex Campaign Management module within Webex Contact Center. Learners will configure and optimize outbound communication campaigns using Control Hub, focusing on agent-assisted and agentless IVR campaigns. Participants will practice key tasks such as dialing schedule management, contact list handling, applying suppression rules, and enforcing compliance settings to ensure effective and regulatory-compliant campaign execution.

Upon completion of this lab, you will be able to test the webex campaign calls.

docs.title: Before You Begin: Lab Login & Testing Instructions
1. Log in to Cisco Control Hub
docs.text: Before starting the lab tasks, retrieve your Control Hub login credentials from your assigned lab session by simply connecting to workstation webRDP and it will have all the sessions details, in case you don’t find those details use below logic:

docs.text:
1. Open your assigned lab session.
  2. Navigate to the Info tab.
  3. Locate the DNS entry details.

Example DNS entry:

mail1.cb476.dc-01.com

Your Organization domain is the DNS entry without the mail1. prefix.

Organization domain: cb476.dc-01.com

docs.title: Step 2: Determine Your Username
docs.text:
The administrator username is the same for all lab sessions:

cholland

Use the following format to construct your Control Hub login username:

cholland@<org-domain>

Example:

docs.title: Step 3: Determine Your Password
docs.text:
Your password is generated using your assigned Session ID.

Password format: its same for both Control hub and Agent login

Replace XXXX with the last four digits of your Session ID.

Example:

docs.title: Step 4: Sign In
docs.text:
1. Open Cisco Control Hub using the lab-provided URL.
  2. Enter your generated username.
  3. Enter your session-specific password.
  4. Complete the sign-in process.

Note: Use the credentials corresponding to your assigned lab session.

docs.title: 2. Lab Testing: Verify the Call Flow
docs.text: The lab workstations have the Webex app configured with phone service, which can be used to test your lab configuration.

docs.title: Testing Procedure
docs.text:
1. Open the Webex app on the lab workstation.
  2. Navigate to the dial pad.
  3. Dial the assigned channel number.
  4. Verify that the call connects successfully.
  5. Follow the configured call flow and validate the expected prompts, menu options, routing, and call handling.

Expected Result: The call should follow the configured call flow and behave as expected based on your lab setup.

docs.title: Learning Objectives
docs.text:
Upon completion of this lab, you will be able to:

  • Create the routing objects behind an inbound call in Webex Contact Center: a team, a queue, and business hours.
  • Build a multi-branch IVR in Flow Designer using Business Hours, Menu, Collect Digits, Play Message, Set Variable, Condition, Queue Contact, and Play Music activities.
  • Use a flow variable and expressions to limit menu retries.
  • Validate and publish a flow, then link it to a phone number through a channel.
  • Sign in to Agent Desktop with WebRTC (browser voice) and test every caller path end to end.

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text:
In this lab you build the phone system for Cisco Live Coffee Co., a coffee shop at the event. Customers call one number. The IVR must:

  • Check whether the shop is open.
  • Offer a main menu: 1 for order status, 2 to talk to a barista, 3 for store information.
  • For order status, collect a 5-digit order number and read it back.
  • For a barista, queue the call to your agent team with hold music.
  • Give the caller one retry after a wrong key or no input, then end the call politely on a second failure.

You build every object yourself, from the team to the channel. Then you sign in as an agent in Agent Desktop and place test calls from your mobile phone.

Naming rule: your instructor assigns a learner ID, such as L01. Replace L01 with your ID in every name. Use uppercase and underscores, with no spaces.

docs.title: Task 1: Create the Routing Objects (10 minutes)
docs.text: In this task you create the team that receives calls, the queue that holds callers, and the business hours that the IVR checks.

docs.title: Step 1: Sign in to Control Hub
docs.text:
1. Open Chrome or Edge and go to https://admin.webex.com.
  2. Enter xyz@cb434.dc-01.com and click Sign in.
  3. Enter the password and click Sign in.
  4. In the left menu, under Services, click Contact Center.
  5. If you see only icons, click ☰ at the top left to show the labels.

Note: As mentioned Control logins based on the session which you started so make sure you refer first page for login details of control hub or Agent login.

docs.title: Step 2: Create the team and add the agent
docs.text:
1. Click User management > Teams, then click Create team.
  2. Enter these values:
Field Value Name CL_L01_TEAM Parent site Site-1 Team type Agent based Desktop layout Global Layout (default)
  1. In Agents, type Anita. Tick anita@xyz.wbx.ai in the results, then click empty space to close the list.
  2. Click Create. A green success message confirms the team was created.

docs.title: Step 3: Create the queue
docs.text:
1. Click Customer experience > Queues, then click Create queue.
  2. Enter these values:
Field Value Name CL_L01_QUEUE Channel type Telephony (Inbound) Queue routing type Longest available agent Call distribution Click Create a group. In Group 1, select CL_L01_TEAM only. Click Save Service level threshold 20 seconds Maximum time in queue 300 seconds Default music in queue defaultmusic_on_hold.wav

docs.title: Step 4: Create the business hours

1. Click Customer experience > Business hours, then click Create business hours.
  2. Enter these values:

Verification: Search for each object by name and open it. Check that:

  • CL_L01_TEAM contains the agent.
  • CL_L01_QUEUE Group 1 is CL_L01_TEAM.
  • CL_L01_HOURS covers all 7 days.

docs.title: Task 2: Build the Coffee Co. IVR in Flow Designer (20 minutes)
docs.text:
This is the core of the lab. You add 15 activities, configure them, connect them, and publish the flow.

Before you start the step 1 activity, check below, these are some of the steps you repeat multiple times to read carefully before start creating flow.

Rename an activity: click the activity's title. In the right panel, click the pencil beside Activity label, type the new name, and click ✓. Pressing Enter alone may not save the name.

Add a spoken prompt (TTS):

  1. Turn on Enable text-to-speech.
  2. Set Connector to Cisco Cloud Text-to-Speech.
  3. Click Add text-to-speech message and type the text.
  4. Delete any empty Audio file row with its trash-can icon.

docs.title: Step 1: Create the flow and the variable
docs.text:
1. In Control Hub, click Customer experience > Flows.
  2. Click Manage flows > Create flows, then select Flow > Start fresh.
  3. Name the flow CL_L01_COFFEE_FLOW and click Create flow.
  4. Flow Designer opens in a new tab. If the browser blocks it, allow pop-ups.
  5. Click empty canvas. In the right panel (Global Flow Properties), click Add flow variable and enter:
Field Value Name retryCount Type Integer Default value 0
  1. Click Save.

docs.title: Step 2: Add and configure the activities
docs.text:
For each row below:

  1. Search for the type in the activity library on the left.
  2. Drag the activity onto the canvas. Clicking does not add it.
  3. Rename it to the label shown.
  4. Configure the settings shown.

docs.title: Flow Designer Configuration
docs.text:
# Activity Type Activity Label Configuration 1 Business Hours CheckHours Choose Static business hours.Business Hours: CL_L01_HOURS 2 Menu MainMenu Text-to-Speech (TTS): Configure the prompt as specified below."Welcome to Cisco Live Coffee Co. To check the status of an order, press 1. To speak with a barista, press 2. For store location and hours, press 3."Make Prompt Interruptible: don’t checkCustom menu links: Add three options: 1 – Order Status, 2 – Barista, 3 – Store Info.No-Input Timeout: 5 seconds. 3 Collect Digits OrderNumber TTS: "Please enter your five digit order number, followed by the pound key."Minimum Digits: 5Maximum Digits: 5Terminator: #No-Input Timeout: 5 secondsInter-Digit Timeout: 3 seconds 4 Play Message OrderStatus TTS: "Thank you. Your order number {{OrderNumber.DigitsEntered}} is being prepared and will be ready in about ten minutes. Goodbye." 5 Play Message InvalidOrder TTS: "Sorry, we did not receive a valid five digit order number. Returning to the main menu." 6 Play Message StoreInfo TTS: "We are in the World of Solutions hall, open every day from seven a.m. to seven p.m. Returning to the main menu." 7 Play Message ClosedMsg TTS: "Our store is currently closed. Please call back during business hours. Goodbye." 8 Play Message RetryPrompt TTS: "Sorry, that was not a valid choice. Let's try again." 9 Play Message GoodbyeMsg TTS: "We are having trouble understanding your selection. Please call back later. Goodbye." 10 Play Message BusyMsg TTS: "All of our baristas are busy right now. Please call back in a few minutes. Goodbye." 11 Set Variable IncrementRetry Variable: retryCountValue: {{retryCount + 1}} 12 Condition RetryCheck Expression: {{retryCount < 2}} 13 Queue Contact QueueToBarista Static Queue: CL_L01_QUEUE 14 Play Music HoldMusic Static Audio File: defaultmusic_on_hold.wavDuration: 60 seconds 15 Disconnect Contact DisconnectContact Nothing to configure.

Note: Use the label GoodbyeMsg, not Goodbye. The label Goodbye fails validation as a duplicate.

Tip: In OrderStatus, you can insert the variable with the {x} button instead of typing it.

docs.title: Step 3: Connect the activities
docs.text:
Close the right panel (✕) so it does not cover the canvas. To draw a connection, press and hold on a source output port (the dot on the right edge of the activity) and drag it to the destination's input port (left edge). To remove a wrong connection, click it and press Delete.

# From (Activity) Output Port To (Activity) 1 NewContact out CheckHours 2 CheckHours Working Hours MainMenu 3 CheckHours Holidays ClosedMsg 4 CheckHours Override ClosedMsg 5 CheckHours Default ClosedMsg 6 MainMenu 1 OrderNumber 7 MainMenu 2 QueueToBarista 8 MainMenu 3 StoreInfo 9 MainMenu No-Input Timeout IncrementRetry 10 MainMenu Unmatched Entry IncrementRetry 11 OrderNumber out OrderStatus 12 OrderNumber No-Input Timeout InvalidOrder 13 OrderNumber Unmatched Entry InvalidOrder 14 InvalidOrder out MainMenu 15 StoreInfo out MainMenu 16 IncrementRetry out RetryCheck 17 RetryCheck True RetryPrompt 18 RetryCheck False GoodbyeMsg 19 RetryPrompt out MainMenu 20 QueueToBarista out HoldMusic 21 QueueToBarista Failure BusyMsg 22 HoldMusic out BusyMsg 23 OrderStatus out DisconnectContact 24 ClosedMsg out DisconnectContact 25 GoodbyeMsg out DisconnectContact 26 BusyMsg out DisconnectContact 27 Every Activity Undefined Error DisconnectContact

Click Fit to screen in the bottom toolbar. Check that no output port is left unconnected. DisconnectContact has no outputs.

docs.title: Step 4: Validate and publish
docs.text:
1. Turn on the Validation switch at the bottom right.
  2. Fix every Error. Recommendations can be ignored.
Error Resolution Port not connected Draw the missing line Required field Fill in the field named in the error Duplicate label Rename the activity
  1. When validation shows 0 errors, click Publish Flow.
  2. Enter the comment L01 v1, keep the label Latest, and click Publish Flow.

Verification: In Control Hub, open Flows, refresh, and confirm CL_L01_COFFEE_FLOW shows Published.

docs.title: Task 3: Create the Channel and Sign In the Agent (7 minutes)
docs.text: The channel links the phone number to your flow. The agent must be Available on your team to receive option-2 calls.

docs.title: Step 1: Create the channel
docs.text:
1. In Control Hub, click Customer experience > Channels, then click Create a channel.
  2. Enter these values:
Field Value Name CL_L01_EP Channel type Inbound telephony Service level threshold 20 Timezone Default Routing flow CL_L01_COFFEE_FLOW Music on hold defaultmusic_on_hold.wav Version label Latest
  1. Under Phone numbers, click Add and select:
Field Value Location Site1 PSTN number +14422850953 (This number is just an exmaple, so you will use whatever number is availble while you configure, later same number you use to test) Media region United States (Default)
  1. Click ✓ on the number row, then click Create.

docs.title: Step 2: Sign in to Agent Desktop with WebRTC
docs.text:
Open a new tab and go to https://desktop.wxcc-us1.cisco.com. Sign in as anita@xyz.wbx.ai.

  • Handle calls using: Desktop (WebRTC browser voice)

  • Team: CL_L01_TEAM

  • Click Save.

  • When the browser asks for the microphone, click Allow. Make sure your headset is selected.
  • If the desktop opens without the Station login dialog:
  • Click the avatar at the top right, then Profile Settings.
  • Set Your team to CL_L01_TEAM and click Save.
  • In the state dropdown at the top, choose Available.

Note: username here will be same one which you assigned in Teams. Example: anita@xyz.wbx.ai. Same can be found from contact center Users tab, once you open it will be email address, you can use the same as agent username. For password refer to the first page.

Verification: The desktop shows Available, with team CL_L01_TEAM.

docs.title: Task 4: Test the IVR (8 minutes)
docs.text: Dial +1 442 285 0953 from workstation. Start a new call for each test and use the phone keypad.

docs.title: Step 1: Verify the self-service paths
docs.text: Step Action Result 1 Press 1, enter 12345 The order number is read back, then the call ends 2 Press 1, enter 12 and wait The InvalidOrder message plays, then the main menu returns 3 Press 3 Store information plays, then the main menu returns 4 Press 9, then 9 again First the retry message, then the goodbye message, then the call ends

docs.title: Step 2: Verify the agent path
docs.text:
Step Action Result 5 Agent Available. Press 2 Hold music plays and Agent Desktop rings. Click Accept and confirm two-way audio. Click End, then Submit Wrap Up 6 Agent set to Meeting or Idle. Press 2 About 60 seconds of hold music, then the busy message, then the call ends

Why test 4 ends the call:

  • retryCount starts at 0.
  • The first wrong key sets it to 1. Because 1 < 2, the caller gets a retry.
  • The second wrong key sets it to 2. Because 2 < 2 is false, the goodbye message plays.

docs.title: Step 3: Clean up
docs.text:
1. In Agent Desktop, set the state to Idle.
  2. Tell the instructor you have finished or end the lab once done.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Resolution You hear another learner's IVR or the reference IVR The number is on another channel; move it to CL_L01_EP You hear the closed message Check that CL_L01_HOURS covers all 7 days, 12:00 AM–11:59 PM Your changes are not heard Publish the flow again with the label Latest Order number is not read back Use {{OrderNumber.DigitsEntered}} exactly; the activity label must be OrderNumber Hold music plays but the agent never rings Agent must be Available on CL_L01_TEAM; queue Group 1 must be CL_L01_TEAM No audio on the agent side Allow the microphone (browser padlock icon) and select your headset State changes to Meeting by itself Set it back to Available

docs.title: LABCOL-1712
docs.text:
Webex Contact Center: AI Assistant for Agents Lab

Estimated time: 30 minutes

Before you begin : Once you start the session, First get into workstation web RDP, It will have all session details and CH+User login credentails.

Learning Objectives

Upon completion of this lab, you will be able to:

  • Turn on the Cisco AI Assistant features for Webex Contact Center in Control Hub.
  • Enable real-time transcripts for voice calls by adding one activity to an existing flow.
  • Give agents AI-powered Real-time Assist backed by a simple knowledge base.
  • Use AI-generated mid-call and post-call summaries with suggested wrap-up codes.
  • Explain how call drop summaries, sentiment and Auto CSAT add insight to every interaction.

Telephony outcome sets

A telephony outcome set is a collection of possible call outcomes received from the dialer when an attempt is made to contact a customer. These outcomes indicate whether a call was successfully connected, rejected, busy, or failed for various reasons during the dialing process. The system provides standard telephony outcomes expected from the dialer.

docs.title: 3.- Campaign Management
docs.text: campaign group(s) must be created to deploy a campaign. A campaign group is a ‘wrapper’ within which campaigns are created. A single campaign group can be created to deploy multiple campaigns.

docs.title: 4.- Create Standard Preview Campaign
docs.text:
We will continue to use the nomenclature for campaign identification

“EM_”

Follow these steps to create a campaign group:

  • From the left menu, navigate to Campaign management > Campaign group. The campaign group list screen appears. It will display all the campaigns created in this tenant.

  • Click Create campaign group.
  • On the Create campaign group screen, enter details for the following fields.
  • Campaign group name: Enter a name for the campaign group.
  • Business stakeholder: Enter all the stakeholders for the campaign separated by a comma. For example, Sales Team, Marketing Team, Presales, etc.
  • Reference ID: Enter a unique ID for the campaign group.
  • Campaign image: Add a thumbnail image for the campaign group. The size of the image should not be more than 100 x 100 px. The supported formats are .jpg, .jpeg, .png, .gif, .bmp, and .tif.
  • Description: Enter a description for the campaign group.

Click Save and proceed.

On the recent campaign group created select and open the group

Follow these steps to create a campaign:

On the campaign group list screen, click Create campaign. The campaign configuration screen appears with placeholder nodes to configure.

docs.title: Lab Objective
docs.text: The objective of this lab is to provide hands-on experience with the Webex Campaign Management module within Webex Contact Center. Learners will configure and optimize outbound communication campaigns using Control Hub, focusing on agent-assisted and agentless IVR campaigns. Participants will practice key tasks such as dialing schedule management, contact list handling, applying suppression rules, and enforcing compliance settings to ensure effective and regulatory-compliant campaign execution.

docs.title: Adding user specific variables into your lab guide
docs.text: There may be times in which you want to embed some attendee specific information into the instructions of your lab guide, like credentials or phone numbers, which will be used on multiple pages of your lab guide. You can gather the information via a form or you can pass a pre-encoded JSON string as a URL parameter to populate the variable values into the browser's session storage. Then you can use a simple HTML tag with a special class name to update the values in the lab guide. This feature can be combined with the copy button method above.

docs.title: Form Method
URL Method
docs.text:
If you have a lot of attendee variables in your lab, you may choose to precompile and encode them so that you can simply provide a URL link which will load all of their required information.

docs.title: Initial Setup
docs.text: This lab guide template uses MKDocs to take your markdown documentation and transform it into an interactive web based lab guide. You will need to install some software on your PC or Mac in order to take full advantage of the tool which will allow you to view your changes as you save them and ensure that your formatting is exactly how you want it.

docs.title: Prerequisite Software to Install
docs.text:
1. Python
  2. Visual Studio Code
  3. Git

docs.title: Setting up your lab guide on your computer
Clone your repository with git
docs.text:
Open Visual Studio Code

Click the Source Control button in the left menu

Click Clone Repository

Enter the repository source: {{config.extra.repo}}

Select or create a new folder to clone the repository into.

docs.title: Build the environment
docs.text:
When prompted to open the cloned repository, select open.

Drag open the terminal at the bottom of the Visual Studio Code window

Show Me

If you are on a PCIf you are on a Mac

In your terminal enter the following commands:

python -m venv venv

Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser

venv\Scripts\activate.ps1

pip install -r requirements.txt

mkdocs serve

Open a browser to http://127.0.0.1:8000

In your terminal enter the following commands:

python -m venv venv

source venv/bin/activate

pip install -r requirements.txt

mkdocs serve

Open a browser to http://127.0.0.1:8000

docs.title: Publishing Your Changes
docs.text: As you progress with the creation of your lab guide, you should sync your changes periodically to GitHub.

docs.title: Syncing your changes to GitHub
docs.text:
Make sure that you have saved all of the files you want to sync up to the repository

Click the Source Control button in the left menu

Click the plus sign next to each file you want to sync as you hover over the file names or alternatively, click the plus sign next to changes

Enter a note about the changes you are making in the message text box

Click the down chevron on the commit button to reveal more options

Select Commit & Sync

docs.title: After you Sync your changes, it will take a few minutes for GitHub Actions to build the website so that you can view all of the changes you made.
